newsitem.title: USA: Poll shows Florida sugar tax losing support.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows Florida sugar tax losing support.

text.p: Support for a state constitutional amendment that would impose a $0.01 per lb tax on sugar produced in Florida dropped in the past two weeks, according to a Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel/WTVJ-Ch 6 poll, the newspaper said Friday.
The poll showed that 41 percent opposed the plan, 41 percent favored it and 18 percent were undecided.
A poll two weeks ago showed the measure supported by 49 percent of respondents, according to the newspaper.

The most recent poll was conducted by Mason-Dixon Political/Media Research Inc, which interviewed 828 Florida voters by telephone Monday and Tuesday. Respondents said they voted in most or all statewide elections.
Bob Joffee, vice president with Mason-Dixon, told the Sun-Sentinel the declining support, coupled with the large number of undecided voters, would probably mean the measure would be defeated.
The measure has been the subject of a multi-million barrage of pro and con advertisements by the sugar industry and environmental groups.
